learning.title: The reaper's refuse-shorter-windows rule is load-bearing twice: resume race AND reaping-implies-expiry
learning.body:
From qa-qa's proof on the #514/#517 blob-reaper work (2026-11-17), recorded because the second reason is cheap to state now and expensive to rediscover.
THE INVARIANT: with abandonmentMs >= UPLOAD_SESSION_TTL_MS, the abandonment condition can never reap a session that is not also past expires_at. Proof in three lines: expires_at is set once at session open (created_at + TTL, never extended); the reaper's last-activity bound L >= created_at by construction; abandonment fires when L <= now - abandonmentMs, and abandonmentMs >= TTL gives expires_at = created_at + TTL <= L + TTL <= now. QED.
WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE RESUME RACE: during the #514→#517 inter-merge window, lockUploadSession still carried a denylist that caught reaped sessions only because reaping implies expiry — and reaping implies expiry ONLY because shorter windows are refused, not clamped. Relax the rule (or add a third reap condition not bounded by expires_at) and a session can be reaped with expires_at still future; a denylist guard then ADMITS a part write into a session the reaper already emptied. The rule is not a preference, it is the invariant that keeps every guard over reaped sessions correct — including allowlists that scope expiry to pending, which otherwise read a future expires_at as live.
RULE FOR FUTURE CHANGES: any new reap condition must be provably bounded by expires_at (or the guard family re-verified), and the window validation keeps refusing below-TTL values silently-clamped shortcuts. Two independent reasons, one rule.
